note: Order both products together every 2 days, about 1.05× forecast plus a starting buffer of 15. Main risk: the buffer may be too small, so shortfalls on high-demand days.
Order daily at 1.1× forecast, so less stock and lower storage costs. Main risk: the fixed cost of 45 is paid on 28 days, about 1260 in total.
Every 2 days at 1.2× forecast. A shortage costs 13 per unit against 0.6–0.9 per day to store one, so the bigger buffer pays off. Main risk: higher storage costs and stock expiring.
Order every 3 days, so only 10 ordering fees. Main risk: high storage costs, and the 224-unit capacity could overflow around day 8.
Lean plan: every 2 days, exactly the forecast with no buffer. Main risk: frequent shortages, since average demand runs about 5% above forecast.
Mixed plan: product 0 every 2 days, product 1 in 4-day batches, which works because product 1 keeps for 7 days. Main risk: high storage costs for product 1, plus large single-day demand swings.
Order daily at 1.25× forecast for few shortages. Main risk: 28 ordering fees plus the cost of storing a larger buffer.
Heavy buffer: every 2 days at about 1.35× forecast. Main risk: overflowing the warehouse, stock expiring, and high storage costs.
